# BYOK renewal wire contract evidence

Production correction applied in `ts-orchestrator/cmd/orchestrator/runtime_keylease_renewal.go`.

The Dashboard success response is generated by
`ts-dashboard/src/backend/database/byok-renewal-policy-http.ts` and includes
`allowed`, `status`, `environment`, `tenant_id`, `project_id`, `database_id`,
`admission_operation_id`, `purpose`, `expires_at`, and the full `byok` object.
The Go decoder now requires all of those fields, requires `status` to be
`pending` or `verified`, requires response `purpose` and full BYOK tuple/revision
to equal the request, and retains `json.RejectUnknownMembers(true)`.

The request encoder has no S3 `external_id` or BYOK `backup_external_id` field.
Both are rejected by Dashboard's strict schemas: AWS web identity binds the
workload token's subject, not an external ID. Request and response bodies remain
bounded to 8192 effective bytes (the checker reads max+1 and rejects 8193); the
client has a 20-second timeout and refuses redirects to prevent service-key
forwarding.

Focused source-backed selector:

```text
go test ./cmd/orchestrator -run 'TestRenewalPolicyChecker' -count=1
ok  terras.../cmd/orchestrator  0.112s
```

The tests include the Dashboard response `status`, `purpose`, and full BYOK
tuple, plus exact TLS wire scope, changed tenant/operation, expired and
>30-second decisions, malformed responses, missing status/purpose/BYOK, changed
revision, 8192/8193 response boundaries, and absence of S3 `external_id`.
No provider calls were made. No commits or pushes were made.
